# Data
Load libraries
```{r}
pacman::p_load(sf, # spatial
               here, 
               tidyverse, 
               rio, # for importing
               table1, # make table1
               lubridate,
               ncf, #correlation
               xtable, # export table1
               fuzzyjoin, # joining with some inexact
               spdep, # regression spatial
               tmap, # spatial maps
               sjlabelled, # table 1 labels for sf
               geepack, # for regression
               lme4
               )
```

Read in data
```{r}
## Population of Mérida + Kanasín 
yuc_pop <- read.csv("RESAGEBURB2020 - 31 Yucatán.csv")
## Mérida + Kanasín shapefile from INEGI (eem - Block Polygons)
yuc_m<- st_read(dsn = here("31_yucatan_2020/conjunto_de_datos"),
                    layer = "31m")
yuc_m <- yuc_m %>% 
  filter(CVE_MUN == "041" | CVE_MUN == "050")
## Mérida + Kanasín shapefile from INEGI (eea - Basic Urban Geostatistical Areas)
merida_clean_sf <- st_read(dsn = here("31_yucatan_2020/conjunto_de_datos"),
                    layer = "31a")
merida_clean_sf <- merida_clean_sf %>% 
  filter(CVE_MUN == "041" | CVE_MUN == "050")

## SINAVE case data
season23 <- here::here("data", "SINAVE_Data", 
                       "datos_abiertos_dengue_061223.csv") %>%
  rio::import() %>% 
  dplyr::as_tibble()

## Cases Shapefile
sus <- st_read(dsn = here("data"), 
                 layer = "TIRS_SINAVE_22_23")
sus <- st_transform(sus, st_crs(yuc_m)) # make sure same st_crs
## Cases by TIRS block
sinave_block <- read_csv("data/TIRS_SINAVE_combined22_23_blockID.csv")

## TIRS Clusters Shapefile
clusters_sf <- st_read(dsn = here("data"),
                    layer = "Cluster final 2021 actualizado")
clusters_sf <- st_transform(clusters_sf, st_crs(yuc_m)) # make sure same st_crs
```

## Some Cleaning
Putting all information into the shapefiles
```{r}
# MOH data:
## add CVEGEO to population dataset
yuc_pop_cvegeo <- yuc_pop %>% 
  mutate(CVE_ENT = as.character(ENTIDAD),
         CVE_MUN = paste0("0", MUN),
         CVE_LOC = paste0("000", LOC),
         CVE_AGEB = AGEB,
         CVE_MZA = ifelse(nchar(as.character(yuc_pop$MZA)) == 3, 
                          as.character(MZA),
                          ifelse(nchar(as.character(yuc_pop$MZA)) == 2, 
                                 paste0("0", MZA), paste0("00", MZA))),
         CVEGEO = paste0(CVE_ENT, CVE_MUN, CVE_LOC, CVE_AGEB, CVE_MZA))
yuc_pop_cvegeo <- yuc_pop_cvegeo[-c(1:3),]

## population for all areas of the city (add population numbers to shapefile)
merida_sf <- yuc_m %>% 
  right_join(yuc_pop_cvegeo, by = c("CVEGEO", "CVE_ENT", "CVE_MUN",
                                     "CVE_LOC", "CVE_AGEB", "CVE_MZA"))

# TIRS data -- all cases
cases_sf <- cbind(sus, sinave_block[,c("CVEGEO", "CVE_MZA", "CLUSTER", "MZA3X3",
                                       "MZTIRS", "TIRS")])
```

Only confirmed Dengue 2023 cases
```{r}
# select cases of all the CONFIRMED 2023 dengue cases
s23 <- season23 %>% 
  # only want data for Mérida + Kanasín (050, 041 MUNICIPO_RES)
  filter(MUNICIPIO_RES == 50 | MUNICIPIO_RES == 41) %>% 
  # change symptom onset date to match cases dataset (i.e., weeks since 
  #  start of ABD season)
  mutate(Week_onset = ymd(FECHA_SIGN_SINTOMAS),
         Week_onset = epiweek(Week_onset),
         Year = year(FECHA_SIGN_SINTOMAS)) %>%
  relocate(c(FECHA_SIGN_SINTOMAS, Week_onset), .before = ID_REGISTRO) %>% 
  filter(ESTATUS_CASO == 2) # 1 likely; 2 confirmed; 3 discarded

# from TIRS trial locations, only DENV cases from 2023
denv23 <- cases_sf %>% #674 cases
  filter((str_detect(Diagnosis, "DENV") | str_detect(Diagnosis, "DENGUE"))
         & Year == 2023) %>% # only dengue, only 2023 
  mutate(age_grp = as.factor(ifelse(Age < 18, "Child", "Adult")),
         TIRS = factor(TIRS, levels = c(0, 1), 
                       labels = c("Control", "TIRS Intervention")))
# only adult cases (< 18)
adult_denv23 <- denv23 %>%
  filter(Age >= 18)
# child dengue cases
child_denv23 <- denv23 %>% 
  filter(Age < 18)
```

Number of dengue cases in 2023: `r nrow(denv23)` \\
Number of adult dengue cases in 2023: `r nrow(adult_denv23)`
Number of child dengue cases in 2023: `r nrow(child_denv23)`

# Map
By Intervention, all cases
```{r}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = merida_clean_sf, linewidth = 0.05) +
  geom_sf(data = clusters_sf, linewidth = 0.05, aes(fill = as.factor(TIRS)),
          alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_sf(data = cases_sf, size = 0.25, stroke = 0) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("tomato", "darkolivegreen3"), 
                    name = "TIRS Trial Arm", labels = c("Control", 
                                                        "Intervention")) +
  ggtitle("All Dengue Cases in Trial Geographic Area") + 
  theme_minimal()
ggsave("merida_cases_clusters.pdf")
```

By intervention and age, only Dengue 2023 cases

# Table 1
Formatting
```{r}
### for trial cases
test <- denv23
test$Arm_1TIRS <- 
  factor(test$Arm_1TIRS, levels = c(0, 1),
         labels = c("Control",
                    "TIRS Intervention"))
test$Age <- as.numeric(test$Age)

test$Age <- set_label(test$Age, "Age")
test$Arm_1TIRS <- set_label(test$Arm_1TIRS, "Trial Arm")
test$Week_onset <- set_label(test$Week_onset, "Week of Symptom Onset*")

footnote <- "*Week of the year"

## for all merida cases
s23$SEXO <- 
  factor(s23$SEXO, levels = c(1, 2),
         labels = c("Female",
                    "Male"))
s23$SEXO <- setLabel(s23$SEXO, "Sex")
s23$EDAD_ANOS <- set_label(s23$EDAD_ANOS, "Age")
s23$Week_onset <- set_label(s23$Week_onset, "Week of Symptom Onset*")
```

Make Table 1 for TIRS cases
```{r}
case_tab <- table1(~ Age + Source + Arm_1TIRS + Week_onset, data = test,
       footnote=footnote)
case_tab <- as.data.frame(case_tab)
print(xtable(case_tab, type = "latex"), file = "23denv_case_tab.tex")
```

Table 1 for all city cases of dengue in 2023
```{r}
case_tab_merida <- table1(~ SEXO + EDAD_ANOS + Week_onset, data = s23,
       footnote=footnote)
case_tab_merida <- as.data.frame(case_tab_merida)
print(xtable(case_tab_merida, type = "latex"), file = "23denv_merida_cases_tab.tex")
```

Table 1 for all dengue cases in 2023 (adults and children)
```{r}
table1(~ as.numeric(Age) + TIRS + Week_onset, data = denv23)
```


Table 1 for children and adults
```{r}
# labels
denv23$Week_onset <- set_label(denv23$Week_onset, "Week of Symptom Onset*")
denv23$Age <- as.numeric(set_label(denv23$Age, "Age"))



# table1
by_age_table1 <- as.data.frame(table1(~ Age + TIRS + Week_onset |
                                                     age_grp, data = denv23,
                                                   footnote = footnote,
                                                   render.missing = NULL))
print(xtable(by_age_table1, type = "latex"), 
      file = "by_age_table1.tex")
```

# Cases over time

```{r}
# Cases counts from all of Mérida and the TRIAL
s23_case_counts <- s23 %>% 
  count(Week_onset)

  filter(Source == "TIRS") %>% 
  count(Week_onset) %>% 
  st_drop_geometry()

  count(Week_onset)
```

With same y axis

```{r}
ggplot() +

           aes(x = Week_onset, y = n, fill = "Trial")) +

ggsave("cases_by_week_denv23.pdf")
```

# Case  proportions
```{r}
# make shapefile for the clusters + include population counts
clusters_sf <- st_intersection(merida_sf, clusters_sf)

# Populations of each cluster + block
pop_cluster <- clusters_sf %>% 
  group_by(CLUSTER, MZTIRS) %>% 
  summarize(Block_Population = sum(POBTOT))
pop_block <- clusters_sf %>% 
  group_by(CLUSTER) %>% 
  summarize(Block_Population = sum(POBTOT))
```

Comparing proportion of cases within the study area vs the rest of the city?
```{r}
# All confirmed cases in Mérida caught by MOH / total population of Mérida
nrow(s23) / sum(merida_sf$POBTOT)

# trial area
# num cases in trial / total population of trial area
nrow(denv23) / sum(clusters_sf$POBTOT)
```

# Regression
Oh. Just TIRS?

Clean Data
```{r}
tirs_cohort <- readRDS(file = "all_cases_labeled.rds")

# Okay, now I want all participants, and they get the indicator if their event was dengue in 2023, else 0 (not just first event)
control_clusters <- data %>% group_by(cluster) %>% summarize(trial_arm = mean(trial_arm, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% filter(trial_arm == 0)
data <- tirs_cohort %>% 
  # if pos_all == 0 did not experience event -- censored 
  mutate(Pos_All = ifelse(is.na(Pos_All), 0, Pos_All),
         Dengue = ifelse((denv_case == 1 | denv_chikv == 1 | denv_zikv == 1),
                           1, 0),
         Symp_Date = mdy(var6_symp_date),
         Time2 = if_else(Pos_All == 1 & Symp_Date < Exit_Date, Symp_Date,
                        Exit_Date),
         Age =  year(as.period(interval(start = mdy(rn2_pt_dob), end = Time2))),
         block_id = str_sub(PPID, 3, 4),
         cluster_id = str_sub(PPID, 1, 2),
         trial_arm = ifelse(cluster %in% control_clusters$cluster, 0, 1)) %>% 
  relocate(c(Age, Symp_Date, Time2, Dengue), .after = Exit_Date)  %>%
  # drop missing enrollment/exit dates?
  # also only dengue cases that occurred in 2023
  filter(!is.na(Enrolm_Date)) %>% 
  filter(year(Time2) >= 2023)
```

GEE Regression??
```{r}
# logistic GEE?
gee_block <- geeglm(Dengue ~ trial_arm + rn2_pt_sex + Age,
                  family = poisson,
                  id = block_id,
                  corstr = "exchangeable",
                  data = data)
gee_cluster <- geeglm(Dengue ~ trial_arm + rn2_pt_sex + Age,
                  family = poisson,
                  id = cluster,
                  corstr = "exchangeable",
                  data = data)

summary(gee_block)
# alpha = 0.0786.....not...a lot of within-block correlation?
summary(gee_cluster)
# alpha = 0.0135 also gnsdjfhsdjj no 
```
Mixed-effects logistic regression?
```{r}

                (1 | block_id), family = binomial, data = data)
summary(help) #hmmghdsks

```
